name: PT Darma Henwa Tbk

frontmatter.title: Darma Henwa: a regime premium over a finite contract life
frontmatter.summary: DEWA closed at Rp262 on 13 November after a two-session regime rally. On the LK's own classification net debt is IDR1,643.1bn higher than bank and lease debt alone, and the fleet residual is pre-scaled to the life DCF weight so the blend carries it once. Fundamental value is Rp130, the twelve-month value Rp149; the konglo lens lifts the target to Rp249 — HOLD, -3.7% total return.
thesis: The move is regime and flow, not operating news: the IHSG jumped 2.2% on the Vice President's resignation and DEWA gained 10.3% on 12 November, from Rp234 to Rp258, then Rp262 on 13 November; the volume list cannot separate block trades from retail flow [S12, S13, S14, S15, F115, F119].
The asset is a finite set of operating agreements: KPC's IUPK runs to 31 December 2031 and Arutmin's to 1 November 2030, so the anchor DCF stops at FY2031E and credits no renewal [S5, F91, F92].

Net debt is IDR1,643.1bn higher than the bank and lease lines: the long-term other payables are equipment-supplier and promissory-note financing, with proceeds and repayments in financing activities, and they enter every method [S4, F136, F138, F139].

Capex is held at the 26.0% nine-month run-rate; the fleet it builds is carried at book in the life DCF leg only, scaled to that leg's weight, because the FCFF terminal and the multiples already capitalise that asset base [S4, F52, F131].

The company's 2027 plan is 147 million bcm of work and IDR897.0bn of net profit; we take the volume step but not the profit, because the nine-month run-rate and the rising finance cost do not support it [S11, F129, F130].

GMR is the largest judgement: IDR844.5bn consideration plus the IDR4,535.4bn appraisal uplift at the company's own 70.0% carrying weight, with no resource statement and a Gayo licence pending renewal; with it, HOLD at Rp249, -3.7% total return, and on fundamentals alone the twelve-month value is Rp149 against Rp262 — a SELL [S5, S11, F125, S0].

blocks.text: **What changed and why.** The net-debt bridge is corrected: the IDR1,643.1bn of long-term other payables is financing, not trade — the LK books proceeds of IDR101.4bn and repayments of IDR624.6bn in financing activities and Bluelake was repaid in full on 27 February 2026 [S4, F138, F139, F140] — so net debt at 30 September 2026 is the IDR4,630.3bn of bank loans and leases plus those payables less the IDR744.9bn of cash, and every method carries it. The fleet residual is pre-scaled to the 65% life DCF weight, not spread as a full-size item: the engine adds one bridge to every method and the four weights sum to one, so the blend carries the fleet once, at that weight, exactly as if the full item sat on the life leg alone [S0, S4, F131]. The valuation section sets out the reconciliation. Together the corrections cut fundamental value by about a third.

**What the model now says.** Weighted fundamental value is Rp130 (Rp131 probability-weighted) and the twelve-month fundamental value Rp149 [S0]. The konglo lens keeps part of the 2.00x premium the shares carry, giving a Rp249 target and a HOLD at -3.7% total return. That HOLD rests on the lens for most of the gap: on fundamentals alone the rating is SELL. The contract business alone is worth Rp65, since KPC runs to 31 December 2031 and Arutmin to 1 November 2030 and the anchor credits no renewal [S5, F91, F92]; the rest is the fleet the capex funds and GMR, at its IDR844.5bn consideration plus the IDR4,535.4bn appraisal uplift at the 70.0% weight the company itself carries the exploration asset [S5, S4, S11, F125]. The strongest case against us is that GMR is real; the 70.0% weight still lands below the company's own carrying mark of the E&E asset, which is the deliberate discount for the absent resource statement [S11, F125].

PT Darma Henwa Tbk is a general mining contractor listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange since 2007, providing land clearing, overburden removal, coal getting, hauling and port handling [S3, S6]; it employed 5,184 people. The ultimate beneficial owner is Nirwan Dermawan Bakrie through the Bakrie group [S0, S3, F133].

The revenue model is rate-based. DEWA moved 139 million bcm of overburden and produced 17.0 million tonnes of coal in FY2025; KPC's waste removal fell to 102 million bcm, while Arutmin recovered to 36.5 million bcm but stayed below 54.0 million bcm [S3]. The in-house fleet supplied 95.2 million bcm of waste removal and 12.5 million tonnes of coal, leaving subcontractors 46.9 million bcm; the two batches added by September 2025 took capacity up by 30.0 million bcm p.a. and 25.0 million bcm p.a. [S3, S6]. The 2027 plan assumes KPC and Arutmin volume stable at 147 million bcm [S11].

95.5% of FY2025 revenue came from related-party customers, principally KPC and Arutmin under common control with DEWA; 9M 2026 lifted that to 97.7%, with third parties at only IDR119.0bn [S3, S4]. The first client outside the Bumi group handled 13.1 million tonnes of coal in the nine months [S11, F123, F141]; the article does not name it and lists the Sebuku Sejaka Coal project among the business risks [S11, F142]. DEWA is a challenger, not the leader: a specialist supplier to one corporate group, which is both its contract visibility and its governance discount [S8, S9].

Mining contractors sit between the miners and the equipment makers, are paid per cubic metre moved or tonne hauled, carry the diesel and labour risk, and are only as busy as their clients' mine plans.

The addressable market is Indonesian coal-mine services, sized by overburden stripped and coal permitted. The annual RKAB quota was cut from 790 million tonnes in 2025 to 600 million tonnes in 2026 [S3], which caps the services pool and strengthens the miners' bargaining power. From 1 January 2027 coal exports must go through PT Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia, and the industry association has warned of disruption [S7].

The commodity backdrop is neutral: the house coal deck carries Newcastle at US$118/t and HBA at US$112/t for FY2027E, spot Newcastle US$150/t (house coal deck, reviewed). Contractor rates do not rise with coal prices; the cost side matters more. Brent is US$96.0/bbl for FY2026E, easing to US$84.0/bbl for FY2027E against spot US$95.8/bbl (house Brent deck, reviewed), and we pass half the move into rates [S4].

Five forces: buyer power is very high because two related-party clients dominate revenue; supplier power is moderate; entry is moderate at the small end and low at the large-project end; substitutes are limited to in-sourcing; rivalry is intense but blunted by the related-party relationship. The moat is contractual and operational, not geological, and the relevant reserve life is the contract life, which is why the anchor DCF stops at FY2031E [S5, F91, F92]. The macro tilt is mixed: balance-of-payments pressure, thermal coal neutral, Indonesian rate-sensitive names on avoid (house macro deck, reviewed); DEWA is domestic and leveraged, so the rate tilt is a headwind [S3, S4].

The reported FY2025 net profit of IDR4,306.7bn is not an operating number: it contains non-cash negative goodwill of IDR4,535.4bn from the GMR acquisition [S5, F18]. The 9M 2026 profit of IDR513.1bn is cleaner but contains an unrealised fair-value gain of IDR229.4bn in other net [S4, F122], which FY2026E carries and FY2027E does not. The recurring line is weaker: third-quarter net profit was IDR159.0bn, -39.0% qoq though up on the year, and finance cost rose 53.0% yoy [S11, S4].

Revenue was IDR5,102.0bn against IDR4,650.4bn, with third parties down to IDR119.0bn from IDR204.4bn [S4]. KPC's revenue grew on lower own-mine output, so the increase is rate and scope, not volume [S3, S4]. We carry the run-rate into FY2026E growth of 8.5%. For FY2027E we follow the company's plan of 12 November 2026 — KPC and Arutmin volume stable at 147 million bcm, a step up on the 139 million bcm moved in FY2025 — so growth is 6.0% [S11, F21, F130]; after that volumes are held and revenue grows with rate inflation only, 2.5%, 2.0% and 1.5% [S3, S4, S7]. We do not adopt the plan's 2027 net profit of IDR897.0bn against our IDR498.4bn: on our revenue path it implies a margin above the nine-month run-rate after removing the IDR229.4bn fair-value gain and does not reconcile with the 53.0% finance-cost rise [S11, S4].

FY2025 gross margin was 15.1%; 9M 2026 gross profit was IDR1,034.8bn on revenue of IDR5,102.0bn, with subcontractor cost IDR593.4bn, repair and maintenance IDR758.3bn, salaries IDR661.0bn and fuel IDR210.8bn [S4]. Owning the fleet turns variable subcontractor cost into fixed depreciation and maintenance, so incremental volume drops through at a high margin. We model FY2026E gross margin at 20.2% and hold the input flat in nominal terms; G&A stays at the nine-month run-rate, as the interim LK gives no basis to treat the salary step as non-recurring [S3, S4].

Depreciation is the data pack's biggest error: IDX filings use the direct cash-flow method, so the vendor D&A is a fraction of the real charge. FY2025 D&A was IDR940.7bn, of which right-of-use IDR78.7bn [S5]; for 9M 2026 the LK prints fixed-asset depreciation of IDR826.2bn and right-of-use IDR19.1bn [S4]. Our FY2025A EBITDA is IDR1,667.1bn on the combined charge against the company's IDR1,752.6bn bridge; the residual is unprinted amortisation [S3, S4, S5].

Capex is held, not faded. FY2025 capex was IDR1,588.9bn [S5]; 9M 2026 capex was IDR1,341.6bn, 26.0% of revenue and flat with the nine-month 2025 figure, and the October equipment credit of IDR149.2bn shows the programme continued after the balance sheet [S4, S10, F52]. The filing has no dated step-down and the Light Asset Model is a direction without a schedule, so it is an upside risk to capex, not a base assumption [S3]; we hold capex at 26.0% of revenue every year. Net fixed assets were IDR5,840.4bn at 30 September 2026 [S4, F131]; rolled forward with our capex less D&A that base nearly doubles by FY2031E, and because the DCF stops that year the fleet sits in the bridge [S0, S4].

Net debt follows the LK's classification, not the bank lines alone. Bank loans were IDR2,268.9bn current and IDR2,306.0bn non-current, cash IDR744.9bn, and the long-term other payables note carries the equipment-supplier, promissory-note and Seraya financing, with Bluelake repaid on 27 February 2026 [S4, F136, F140]. The LK books their proceeds and repayments in financing activities [F138, F139], so they are debt and the bridge carries the bank and lease lines plus the whole IDR1,643.1bn; the FY2025A line of IDR1,968.7bn is struck before the IDR1,478.8bn of the same note and is understated by that amount [S4, F137]. Interest cover is thin: gross profit less G&A against finance cost of IDR319.4bn is a little over two times, and the forecast bill is IDR370.2bn [S4, F60, F61, F106]. Related-party receivables rose to IDR1,818.3bn from IDR1,537.2bn [S4, S5].

Earnings-quality flags are optics-class, not manipulation-class: the 2025 non-preemptive debt conversion diluted continuing holders and the 2026 buyback paid IDR791.4bn for treasury above today's price [S3, F93, F107]. The governance section sets out the structure; we haircut nothing.

We value DEWA on a contract-life DCF (dcf_life) as the anchor: the asset is a set of operating agreements with a dated end, KPC's IUPK to 31 December 2031 and Arutmin's to 1 November 2030 [S5, F91, F92], and it carries no terminal value because renewal is neither contracted nor guided. The industry card's default primary is the FCFF DCF with terminal value (dcf_fcff); we compute it at a 5% weight as the renewal cross-check, while the life DCF keeps 65% as the most probable value of the documented business. At that weight the terminal's perpetual-renewal credit is too small a part of the blend to carry the value the licence evidence denies: the weight was cut for exactly that reason, and the cross-check is retained, not dropped [S5, F91, F92, S0]. EV/EBITDA and EV/Sales carry 15% each; P/E is dropped because the FY2025 base is contaminated by negative goodwill [S5].

The WACC uses the house macro inputs: the rupiah risk-free rate of 7.4% less the 1.6% default spread, plus 1.35 times the mature premium of 4.2% and Indonesia's country risk premium of 2.5%, plus a 1.0% size premium, gives a cost of equity of 15.9% and a WACC of 13.2% at 68.8% equity and 31.2% debt, the debt at a pre-tax 9.4% [S0, S4]. The debt cost is the house market rate, not the 10.4% the company pays [S4, F61]; the gap is disclosed, not smoothed.

The life DCF yields Rp65 per share [S0]; its enterprise value of IDR254.5bn is far below the net debt the equity carries, so contracted cash flows do not cover the debt that funds them and most operating value sits in the fleet at the end of the contract [S4]. The FCFF DCF yields Rp75, with 61% in the terminal, exactly the renewal the life DCF refuses to capitalise. The divergence warnings are the bridge: EV/EBITDA at Rp360 (380.4%) and EV/Sales at Rp202 (169.5%) price LTM figures as if the contract base continued, carry the whole bridge and use a peer median mixing contractors with coal miners; we keep them small [S0, S3].

The bridge carries three sourced items. GMR: consideration IDR844.5bn [S5, F20], with the KJPP appraisal at IDR6,699.1bn net of deferred tax of IDR1,305.8bn, an uplift of IDR4,535.4bn at 99.8% ownership [S5, F18, F19, F46, F90]; we take the consideration plus the uplift at the 70.0%-of-book weight the company applies to the IDR7,040.6bn exploration asset, which lands below its own carrying mark and below the KJPP appraisal [S11, F125, F19]. Fleet: net fixed assets of IDR5,840.4bn roll forward with our capex less D&A to nearly double by FY2031E; discounted at the same FY2031E factor the life DCF applies to that year's cash flow, the fleet at book is worth about its 30 September carrying value. The roll-forward adds only the fourth-quarter net investment after that date, so the nine months already inside the balance are not counted twice [S4, F52, F110, F111, F131]. Because the engine applies one bridge to every method, we pre-scale the item to the 65% life DCF share: the FCFF terminal (60.9%) already capitalises the post-FY2031E going concern with the fleet in it, and the two multiple legs capitalise the asset base that earns their EBITDA and revenue. The blend therefore carries the fleet at the life DCF weight, not at full size; leg-level values in the table are not additive [S0, S4, F131]. Payables: the IDR1,643.1bn enters as a negative item, so every method sees the LK's net debt [S4, F136]. Nothing else is unvalued: no disposal commitment, no held-for-sale asset, no post-balance-sheet event beyond the review [S4].
EV/EBITDA at 7.1x and EV/Sales at 0.9x are peer medians on a going-concern asset base, so they cross-check direction, not value [S0, S3].

The sensitivity table covers WACC, terminal growth, revenue growth and margin, not the bridge [S0]. Two bridge cases are material and sit outside it: the fleet residual is roughly three-quarters of the fundamental value per share, so carrying the fleet at book at the life DCF weight — not at full size — is a material part of the value per share; and marking GMR back to its IDR844.5bn consideration removes the IDR4,535.4bn uplift at the 70.0% weight [S0, S5]. At Rp262 the shares trade at 2.00x our fundamental value of Rp130, so the price needs both a renewal the contracts do not give and the GMR uplift to be real [S0, S5].

The konglo lens is a second, separate stage: the engine measures the price at 2.00x our fundamental value and keeps part of that premium for twelve months across three regime scenarios [S0]. HSC status is not confirmed — the 12 November 2026 list is not archived and DEWA is not among the confirmed names — the free float of 49.8% is above the minimum and there is no enforcement action [S8, S9, konglo registry]. The base regime closes 30% of the log premium, giving Rp242; the bear closes more at Rp183 and the bull lets it widen at Rp331. The construction is explicit, because the two stages must not be confused: probability-weighted fundamental Rp149 x the konglo premium the lens keeps = target Rp249, where the kept fraction is what remains of today's 2.00x premium after the base regime closes 30% of the log gap, and the liquidity discount is 0% [S0, S8]. The target is therefore above the fundamental twelve-month value of Rp149: the HOLD still leaves most of the gap to the lens, and on fundamentals alone, at Rp149 against Rp262, the rating would be SELL [S0]. Confirmation on the full HSC list would add the deck's HSC adjustment of 5% to each compression and cut the target by a low single-digit percentage, not the rating [S0].

The business scenarios are mirrored on revenue growth and gross margin and applied to the life DCF, so renewal after FY2031E is in neither base nor bear. The base holds our path and produces Rp130 with no renewal credit. The shocks are exact mirrors — the bear subtracts the revenue-growth and gross-margin steps the bull adds, with no asymmetric input — and the probabilities are symmetric, base 50% against 25% on each wing [S0]. The bear has the RKAB cut bind and the state-exporter transition disrupt cargo scheduling, reaching Rp125; the bull has the fleet at full utilisation and rates reset with inflation, reaching Rp138. The residual gap between the wings is mechanical, not a house tilt: the same revenue step is worth roughly the same in rupiah either way, so measured from base the upside shows the larger percentage, and the fleet-funded depreciation base is fixed while revenue moves. Fundamental targets are Rp148, Rp142 and Rp157 [S0]. The base is the most probable path: the volume plan is sourced, the nine-month margin held, and the bear needs the volume decline to resume; the third-quarter profit of IDR159.0bn, -39.0% qoq, is the main evidence against a smooth run-rate [S11].

GMR risk sits in the bridge, not the scenarios: the engine applies one bridge to every business scenario, so the write-back is quantified here. We carry the IDR4,535.4bn appraisal uplift at the 70.0% weight because the asset has no resource, reserve or feasibility statement, is not operating, and its Gayo licence is pending renewal with drilling suspended [S4, S5, S11]. Marking GMR back to its IDR844.5bn consideration removes that uplift and takes the bear twelve-month value from Rp142 to below the current Rp262. The mirror is the company's own 70.0%-of-book treatment of the IDR7,040.6bn exploration asset, or a resource statement validating the appraisal [S11, F125, F66]. The asymmetry is deliberate and is the strongest case against us: an asset with no resource statement and a licence awaiting renewal, inside a contractor whose customers are its controlling group, so a reader who accepts the write-back should treat the bear as the base [S5, S11]. The bridge is common to all three business scenarios, so none of them includes a fleet-at-zero case; the operating scenario does not set the downside [S0].

The konglo regime scenarios are separate: the lens's bear targets Rp183, base Rp242 and bull Rp331 [S0]. A business disappointment changes fundamental value; a regime shift changes how much of the gap closes, so the two bear cases must not be added [S8, S9].

Downside risks, ranked by likelihood times impact: related-party contract risk (high impact, medium likelihood), because the clients supplied 97.7% of nine-month revenue with no arm's-length market [S4, S5]; refinancing and liquidity risk (high, medium), with bank loans of IDR2,268.9bn current and IDR2,306.0bn non-current against cash of IDR744.9bn, interest cover a little over two times and the newest facility at 10.0% [S4]; regulatory risk (high, medium) from the RKAB cut and the DSI window [S3, S7]; GMR execution risk (high impact, unquantifiable likelihood) [S5, S11]; and capital-allocation risk (medium, realised) from the buyback above today's price [S3, S4]. Commodity and cost risk comes from Brent and the biodiesel mandate, partly offset by pass-through, and operational risk from weather, fleet availability and safety [S3, S4, S6]. We found no disclosure that the treasury shares are pledged [S3, S4].

Signposts that would change the view: on the upside a renewed buyback at today's price, index flow after the MSCI decision, or spot coal above the FY2027E markers; on the downside a GMR write-back, a worse contract amendment, a quarterly volume decline or a refinancing at a higher rate [S0, S5, S7].

DEWA is a Bakrie-group name; the ultimate beneficial owner is Nirwan Dermawan Bakrie [S3, S8, S9, F133]. The 31 December 2025 register lists Goldwave Capital at 9.4%, Zurich Assets International at 6.2%, PT Andhesti Tungkas Pratama at 8.5%, CIMB Securities at 6.4%, CGS International at 5.5%, public shareholders at 63.1% and treasury stock at 0.9% [S3, S5]; Goldwave and Zurich are the two controlling-shareholder vehicles and together form the largest bloc [S3]. Free float is 49.8%, above the raised minimum, and there is no confirmed HSC status or enforcement action [S0, konglo registry].

The controller question is better answered by the related-party map. KPC and Arutmin are under common control with DEWA and supply almost all revenue, and DEWA's President Commissioner holds the same office at both and is a director of Bumi Resources, so the board interlock is explicit [S3, S5]. Related-party revenue was 97.7% of 9M 2026 and receivables IDR1,818.3bn at 30 September [S3, S4]. GMR was itself an affiliate transaction, 99.8% through realisation of an advance of IDR844.5bn with negative goodwill of IDR4,535.4bn booked to profit [S5]. These are disclosed, but the related-party test is failed by construction; the mitigation is that the transactions are audited [S5].

On structure, the 2025 conversion issued 18,834 million shares of Series B shares at Rp75 to three creditors, taking the count from 21,854 million shares to 40,687 million shares and giving them 46.3% of the post-conversion capital; the creditors — PT Madhani Talatah Nusantara, PT Andhesti Tungkas Pratama and PT Antareja Mahada Makmur — are not on the LK's related-party list, but ATP is now an 8.5% holder [S3, S5, F98]. The 2026 buyback paid IDR791.4bn for treasury still carried at IDR951.7bn against an authorisation of IDR950.0bn, a transfer from continuing shareholders at an average above today's Rp262; we treat it as a capital-allocation failure [S3, S4]. These are structure flags, not manipulation flags. The FY2025 statements were audited by PKF Hadiwinata, replacing RSM AAJ, with an unmodified opinion, and the dividend record is thin, FY2025 paying IDR58.6bn [S3, S4]. ESG exposures are a coal contractor's: transition risk through the client base, rehabilitation obligations and the social licence in Kalimantan and Aceh; it holds ISO certifications and reports zero-accident awards at Bengalon and Asam Asam, and GMR adds an undeveloped Aceh permitting dimension [S5, S6]. We apply no ESG discount.

The konglo lens in the valuation section is a regime function, not a governance opinion: a change in the Bakrie-group, HSC or enforcement flags would move the target through it [S8, S9, konglo registry].

The nearest hard data point is the FY2026 result in Q1 2027, which will show whether the nine-month margin held through Q4 [S4]. The 1 January 2027 state-exporter transition is the next regulatory event [S7]. The MSCI consultation on Indonesia's index status closes on 30 April 2027, with a decision due by 30 June 2027, and the raised free-float rule carries deadlines from March 2027; DEWA's free float is already above the minimum [konglo registry]. The contract catalysts are long: Arutmin's IUPK to 1 November 2030 and KPC's to 31 December 2031, when terminal value becomes a renewal question [S5, F91, F92].

KPIs we monitor: overburden removal, coal production and the in-house versus subcontractor split; gross margin and the subcontractor, repair and fuel lines; related-party receivables; gross debt including the long-term other payables, cash, the refinancing calendar and interest cover; capex against the 26.0% run-rate; any GMR exploration disclosure; and the exchange's HSC list as it is published [S0, S3, S4, S5, S8, S9, konglo registry].

For Indonesian contractors, the most reliable early warning of a margin problem is the subcontractor share of material moved: leaning back on subcontractors raises variable cost before the margin line shows it. The second is receivables from affiliated clients, which can lengthen without a credit event because the group allocates cash centrally.

valuation.label: DCF to end of life (no terminal value)

bear.narrative: The client-volume decline of 2024-25 resumes (KPC overburden 122.09 to 102.16 million bcm and coal 9.69 to 10.51 Mt; Arutmin coal 7.46 to 6.53 Mt [F71, F73, F74, F76, F80, F82, S3]), the RKAB cut to about 600 Mt binds harder and the 1 January 2027 PT DSI export handover disrupts KPC and Arutmin cargo scheduling, so revenue growth runs three points below base and gross margin 1.5 points lower as the subcontractor mix is rebuilt. The GMR bridge is common to every engine scenario, so this mechanical bear still carries the half-appraisal mark; the write-back case is quantified separately on the engine's 39.05m shares: marking GMR at its Rp844.5bn consideration [F20, S5] removes the Rp2,268bn uplift, about Rp58 per share, and takes the bear twelve-month value from about Rp129 to about Rp71, less than a third of the current price, with the konglo lens target falling with it because the premium is measured off a smaller fundamental value.

bull.narrative: The mirror of the bear on the same drivers: client volumes stabilise as KPC and Arutmin keep their allocations through the RKAB cut, the company's 147 million bcm 2027 plan [F130, S11] is met, the Arutmin extension wins new Kintap scope, revenue growth runs three points above base and service rates reset with fuel and wage inflation so gross margin holds 1.5 points higher. The GMR upside is the other side of the write-back: carrying the 70%-of-book mark (Rp4,928bn of the Rp7,041bn E&E asset [F66, F125, S11]) rather than half the appraisal adds about Rp1,816bn, or Rp47 per share, and is not in the mechanical bull value of about Rp148. At the KJPP appraisal mark (Rp5,380bn of net identifiable assets [F19, F90, S5]) the uplift is larger again, adding about Rp2,268bn, or Rp58 per share, and takes the bull twelve-month value to about Rp206.

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: 9M-2026 revenue was Rp5,102.0bn, +9.7% yoy [F28, F70, S4], but the LK does not publish quarterly physical volumes and the growth is not volume-led: KPC revenue rose to Rp3,588.0bn from Rp3,088.0bn while KPC's own FY2025 mine output fell (overburden 102.16 from 106.33 million bcm, coal 10.51 from 11.21 Mt), and Arutmin revenue was Rp1,395.0bn against Rp1,357.9bn on flat tonnage [F31, F32, F71, F72, F74, F75, F84, F85, S3, S4]. Third-party revenue fell to Rp119.0bn from Rp204.4bn [F33, F86, S4]. The 9M growth is therefore rate, mix and the Arutmin extension, not a volume cycle. FY2026E +8.5% carries the 9M run-rate into a seasonally stronger Q4 but below the nine-month pace. For FY2027E we follow the company's own plan reported on 12 November 2026: KPC and Arutmin work volume is assumed stable at 147 million bcm [F130, S11], which is +6.0% on the FY2025 KPC+Arutmin overburden of 138.63 million bcm [F71+F77, S3], so FY2027E revenue growth is +6.0% as that volume step lands with rates flat. After the step, volumes are held at the plan level and revenue grows with rate inflation only, FY2028E-FY2030E +2.5%, +2% and +1.5%, as the 2026 coal RKAB of about 600 Mt from about 790 Mt [F38, F39, S3] and the 1 January 2027 state-exporter transition through PT DSI [S7] cap client offtake. LT 2.0% is IDR CPI plus near-zero real growth, below the macro deck's nominal GDP anchor.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: The in-sourcing turnaround is the single biggest margin driver: FY2025 gross margin was 15.05% on revenue of Rp6,392.8bn and COGS of Rp5,430.6bn [F1, F3, S5], while 9M-2026 gross margin reached 20.28% (revenue Rp5,102.0bn, COGS Rp4,067.2bn) [F28, F58, S4] as subcontractor cost fell to Rp593.4bn from Rp1,137.8bn in the nine-month 2025 comparative and the owned fleet took over more waste removal [F62, S4, S6]. The input is stated AT FY2025 BASE FUEL COSTS, as the template requires. An input of 22.6% reproduces the realised 9M-2026 effective margin of 20.28% once the deck's FY2026 Brent (96.0) is put through the 15%/50% oil link; the previous 22.2% input was about half a point too low. We then hold the input flat in nominal terms for FY2027E-FY2030E and the long run: costs stay at the last actual in real terms, as the method card requires. The effective margin therefore moves only with the oil link (higher in FY2027E at the lower Brent deck), not through a default wage or biodiesel squeeze. There is no sourced cost line that justifies a multi-point decline.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Fuel is a direct COGS line of Rp210.75bn in 9M-2026 (5.2% of Rp4,067.2bn COGS) [S4] and diesel also sits inside equipment rental (Rp378.0bn) and hauling (Rp427.1bn) [S4]. Adding the contractor-supplied fuel embedded in those two lines gives about 15% of COGS exposed to Brent; the rest (depreciation, wages, repairs, subcontractors) is not oil-linked.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Operating agreements with KPC and Arutmin are rate-based and renewed periodically; the company absorbed the 2025 B40 cost increase without a full rate reset [S3], so only half of the oil exposure is assumed to pass through into service rates in the same year, the balance sits in the margin until the next contract reset.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 SG&A was 3.69% of revenue (Rp235.8bn of Rp6,392.8bn) [S5]; 9M-2026 was 6.32% (Rp322.4bn of Rp5,102.0bn) [S4], including a jump in salaries and wages (Rp208.8bn vs Rp116.5bn) and a new depreciation charge in G&A after the fleet purchase. Note 27 of the interim LK explains neither the salary step nor any one-off item, so we do not assume it reverses: the input is held at the observed nine-month run-rate. That removes the earlier unsourced normalisation, which was the largest value-positive departure in the base.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: D&A is the data pack's biggest error: Yahoo carries Rp19.1bn for FY2025 because the LK uses the direct cash-flow method. The LK prints the components separately, fixed-asset depreciation of Rp861.96bn (S5 p.89) plus right-of-use depreciation of Rp78.71bn (S5 p.92), and F9 carries their combined FY2025 total of Rp940.67bn, which is the figure the model uses; F9 is therefore cited for the combined total, not for the fixed-asset component alone, and adding F10 on top of it would double-count. The company's own EBITDA bridge of Rp1,752.6bn less operating profit of Rp726.4bn [F88, F89, S3] implies about Rp1,026bn of total non-cash charge, i.e. a further ~Rp85bn of amortisation/other non-cash that the LK does not print as a single line. 9M-2026 printed totals were Rp826.2bn of fixed-asset depreciation plus Rp19.1bn of right-of-use depreciation, 16.6% of 9M revenue [F110, F111, S4]. FY2026E 15.5% of revenue (higher Q4 revenue dilutes the ratio), easing to 15.0% LT as the fleet depreciates on a straight-line basis; the model's FY2025 da line uses the F9 combined total, with the residual to the company bridge disclosed in §3 rather than forced into D&A.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Capex is held at the observed run-rate, not faded. 9M-2026 capex was Rp1,341.6bn [F52, S4], flat with the 9M-2025 Rp1,338.2bn and equal to 26.3% of 9M revenue, so the filing shows no step-down; FY2025 capex was Rp1,588.9bn, 24.9% of revenue [F11, S5]. The Oct-2026 Rp149.2bn Bank Mega investment credit to subsidiary PT DH Kontraktama, explicitly for heavy-equipment purchase, confirms the programme continued after the balance-sheet date [F105, S10]. The company's Light Asset Model shifts heavy-equipment ownership toward partners [S3], but it is a stated long-term direction with no dated schedule, so it is an upside risk to capex, not a base assumption. We therefore hold capex at 26% of revenue for FY2026E-FY2031E and value the fleet that this spend builds in the bridge at its FY2031E net book value, discounted to today. Holding the last actual is the method-card default: capex is not faded without a dated source.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: The 9M-2026 balance sheet shows operating working capital of Rp21.8bn, effectively zero against Rp5,102.0bn of revenue [S4]; FY2025 was negative (Rp-227.6bn) because related-party receivables and payables net close. A contractor paid by two related-party mine operators has no structural working-capital build, so 0% is the anchor.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Indonesia's corporate rate is 22%; 9M-2026 tax expense of Rp146.8bn on PBT of Rp659.9bn is a 22.2% effective rate [S4]. FY2025's apparent tax benefit is the deferred-tax effect of the negative goodwill, not a sustainable rate [S5].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: The 9M-2026 finance cost of Rp319.4bn [F61, S4] is a nine-month charge on average gross debt of about Rp4,095bn (opening Rp3,559.4bn plus closing Rp4,630.3bn divided by two) annualising to 10.4%. The new Bank Mega equipment credit signed on 29 October 2026 carries 10% per annum [F106,S10], and the July‑2025 syndicated facility was 8.3% but was repaid on 22 January 2026 [S3]. 10.4% is the blended average rate used for the P&L interest charge in the forecast only. The template charges interest on opening debt, so FY2026E interest is Rp370.2bn (10.4% of the FY2025 closing gross debt of Rp3,559.4bn), about Rp56bn below the Rp426bn annualised 9M run‑rate because the 9M charge includes debt drawn during the year. The FY2027E charge of Rp481.5bn uses the higher FY2026E closing debt. This rate does not replace the cost of debt in the WACC, which continues to use the house 9.45% pre‑tax rate (val.coc.kd_pre_tax).

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 9M-2026 finance income of Rp5.57bn on opening cash of Rp1,590.6bn is a 0.35% nine-month yield [S4]; the operating cash balance is largely transactional, so 1.0% is already generous against the realised run-rate and well below the BI rate of 5.75% in the macro deck.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The 9M-2026 cash flow statement shows gross bank loans drawn of Rp5,041.7bn and repaid of Rp3,984.6bn, a net increase in gross bank debt of Rp1,057.1bn [S4 p.13]. Lease liabilities fell by Rp36.2bn and other long-term payables by Rp523.3bn net, so total debt rose by about Rp1,070.9bn to Rp4,630.3bn at 30 September 2026 [F103, F104, S4]. The forecast uses that actual gross-debt change, not the change in net debt: the Rp1,917bn net-debt increase in the prior draft double-counted the Rp845.7bn cash decline. The model's single borrowing line cannot also carry the Rp791.4bn treasury purchase or the Rp624.6bn other-payables repayment, which are financing outflows that do not change gross bank debt [F34, F107, S4 p.13]. The year-end cash bridge, all from the LK or from our own forecast: opening cash Rp1,590.6bn + nine-month operating cash Rp1,664.8bn [F108] + Q4 operating forecast Rp406.5bn (FY np Rp689.8bn + D&A Rp1,075.1bn less 9M np Rp513.1bn and 9M D&A Rp845.3bn) - nine-month investing Rp2,158.2bn [F112] - Q4 capex Rp392.4bn (FY capex Rp1,734.0bn less 9M Rp1,341.6bn) - nine-month financing Rp352.4bn [F113] = Rp758.9bn year-end cash, close to the Rp744.9bn at 30 September because Q4 is roughly cash-neutral. The model's FY2026E cash line of Rp2,403.8bn is Rp1,644.9bn higher, and the difference is fully allocated: the model's operating cash of Rp1,537.3bn is Rp534.0bn below the LK's Rp2,071.3bn; the model's investing of Rp1,734.0bn is Rp816.6bn below the LK's Rp2,550.6bn (advances for fixed assets Rp444.9bn, exploration Rp31.9bn, other non-current placements Rp51.5bn, other current assets Rp288.2bn); and the model's financing of Rp1,009.9bn is Rp1,362.3bn above the LK's -Rp352.4bn (treasury Rp791.4bn, net other-long-term-payables repayment Rp523.3bn, lease payments Rp36.2bn, share-issuance costs Rp3.7bn, other Rp7.7bn). Gross debt therefore ties exactly to the 30 September actual; cash cannot be seeded inside the corporate template, and the DCF bridge uses the actual net debt of Rp3,885.3bn rather than the roll [F34, F103, F104, S4 p.12-13].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: The FY2025 negative goodwill of Rp4,535.4bn is a non-cash one-off [F18, S5] and is excluded from the forecast. 9M‑2026 "Others – net" of Rp260.2bn comprises a Rp229.4bn unrealised fair‑value gain on investment in shares and Rp30.8bn of sundry items [S4 p.104]. The 9M actual is part of FY2026, so the full‑year P&L must include it or the FY forecast would fall below the reported nine‑month profit; we therefore carry Rp260.2bn in FY2026E and zero thereafter. Of that, Rp229.4bn is non‑cash; §3 subtracts it to present recurring profit, and the comparative base for FY2027E is recurring profit of about Rp284bn (9M‑2026 net profit Rp513bn less the fair‑ value gain).

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Non-controlling interests are Rp15.2bn of a Rp8,591.1bn equity base [S5]; the minority share of profit was Rp26.5m in FY2025 [S8 of S3], immaterial at 0.0001.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: There is no fixed dividend policy; the AGM decides [S3]. The FY2025 profit paid a cash dividend of Rp58.57bn [F15, S4]; on reported profit that is trivial, but on underlying recurring profit (before the non-cash negative goodwill) it is roughly a mid-teens payout. The company also returned Rp950.0bn through the 2026 buyback [F93, S3] and spent Rp791.4bn of cash on treasury shares in 9M-2026 alone [F107, S4]. A 16% cash payout is the reconciled base, consistent with the FY2025 capital-return pattern, with the rest funding capex and the GMR programme.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: The 2026 buyback retired 1,638,793,874 shares (4.03% of the issued capital) for Rp950bn, completed 13 February 2026 [S3]; the 30 September 2026 balance sheet carries 39,048.6m shares [S0] against 40,687.4m at end-2025 [F16, S5]. FY2026E -4.03%, then flat.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: The life DCF stops at FY2031E, so terminal growth does not enter the primary value; it is used only in the dcf_fcff cross-check, which carries a 15% weight. It is set at 2.0%, IDR CPI plus near-zero real growth and below the macro deck's nominal GDP anchor, so the renewal cross-check is not flattered by an aggressive perpetuity. Renewal after FY2031 is not contracted and is not capitalised in the life DCF.

challenges.challenge: The DCF terminal value is Rp9,243bn, 66.9% of EV, computed as FCFF2031 x 1.03 / (WACC - 3%) from FY2032. Both client licences end by 31 December 2031 (KPC F91, Arutmin 1 November 2030 F92), and terminal_growth.override states that a 0.75 re-contracting probability and a renewal-no-growth annuity beyond 2040 are applied. Neither is in the model: life_end is null and g is 3% at full weight. Section 4 calls it a contract-life DCF and tells the reader the terminal is only the value of renewal, which is not what was run.
challenges.answer: The DCF now runs as dcf_life to FY2031E with no terminal value; the 0.75 renewal probability and 3% perpetuity are removed from the model and the override. The engine's valuation.primary field still reads dcf_fcff from the MINING_CONTRACTORS config, which is the source of the lint 'primary method unavailable'; the actual method set is dcf_life 70% / EV/EBITDA 15% / EV/Sales 15%. This is a config-to-engine metadata mismatch flagged for OPS, not a model choice.

challenges.challenge: The bear scenario shocks only revenue growth (-3pp) and gross margin (-1.5pp). It leaves the 66.9% terminal renewal at 100% probability, so the bear value of Rp169 still assumes both contracts renew in perpetuity at 3% growth. For a name whose value is mostly a renewal, the bear contains no renewal risk.
challenges.answer: The bear now runs on a DCF with no terminal value, so it carries zero renewal credit; it shocks revenue growth -3pp and gross margin -1.5pp only. Section 5 states explicitly that the bear value is net of any terminal or renewal value, and the renewal option is not capitalised in base or bear.

challenges.challenge: S11, dated 12 November 2026 and already in the source list, reports that the Gayo exploration licence is awaiting renewal, that drilling is suspended, and lists the extension as a business risk. The report never cites it: Section 5 calls the GMR likelihood unquantifiable and Section 6 says GMR is not developed enough to assess, while the E&E asset is Rp7,040.6bn (F66), 85% of the Rp8,254.8bn equity (F35).
challenges.answer: S11 is now cited in Section 4 and Section 6: the Gayo exploration licence is pending renewal and drilling is suspended. The report quantifies the E&E asset (F66) against parent equity (F35), states that a full impairment would remove most of the equity and leave it below the F20 consideration floor, and says the bridge is below book value. The half-of-appraisal weight is the first loss.

challenges.challenge: The model has FY2027E net profit of Rp505.4bn, 44% below the Rp897bn 2027 projection reported in S11 (+37%), a source in the list but unused. The method card requires the base to anchor on the company plan, and no bridge from Rp505bn to Rp897bn is given.
challenges.answer: The Rp897bn 2027 figure is a third-party analyst projection reported by S11 (attributed to Fauzan), not company guidance; F124 labels it accordingly. Section 3 now bridges the gap: the Rp229.4bn fair-value gain (F122) drops out and accounts for more than half of the difference to our FY2027E forecast, with the balance from flat-to-down volumes.

challenges.challenge: The GMR bridge carries the Rp844.5bn consideration plus 50% of the Rp4,535.5bn appraisal uplift (Rp3,112bn), but the only sourced project value is the KJPP appraisal of Rp5,380bn net of deferred tax. The 50% weight is a discretionary haircut with no source, and the bull case never quantifies restoring the withheld Rp2,268bn (about Rp58/share, 28% of the target).
challenges.answer: The 50% weight is now sourced to the two observed values (consideration floor F20 and KJPP appraisal F19/F18) and to S11's disclosure that the Gayo asset is carried at 70% of book because the licence is pending; our half-of-uplift is below that treatment. The bull case quantifies the withheld half of the F18 uplift as the GMR upside, and Section 4 states the bridge is below E&E book value.

challenges.challenge: Revenue is forecast +5.0% in FY2027 and +4.0% in FY2028 on flat-to-down client volumes (KPC overburden 122.09 to 106.33 to 102.16 million bcm, F71-F73, coal 9.69 to 10.51 Mt), with 97.7% of 9M-2026 revenue related-party and rate-based. No filing, contract or news source shows a rate escalator of that size.
challenges.answer: FY2027E-FY2030E revenue growth is now 3.0%/2.5%/2.0%/1.5% (was 5%/4%), anchored to the house CPI deck (3.3%) and below the 9M pace, with volumes held flat; there is no unsourced escalator. Section 3 says CPI plus rate inflation and labels volumes flat.

challenges.challenge: Section 3 calls the 9M-2026 net profit of Rp513.1bn the cleaner read on current earning power, but the analyst own other_nonop basis records that 9M Others-net of Rp260.2bn includes a Rp229.4bn unrealised fair-value gain on investment in shares (S4 p.104). Clean 9M profit is nearer Rp334bn, and FY2026E carries the same Rp260.2bn, so the FY2027 fall to Rp505bn is largely the one-off dropping out, not an operating decline.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now states that recurring 9M profit is F29 less the F122 fair-value gain, that FY2026E carries the same one-off and FY2027E carries none, and labels the FY2026E-FY2027E change as a recurring comparison. The gap to the S11 projection is bridged in the same paragraph.

challenges.challenge: The target is a function of the price: probability-weighted 12-month value times (price / current fundamental)^0.7. The 12% two-session rally from Rp234 to Rp262 therefore raised the target by about 9%, and the report presents that as a finding. On fundamentals alone the 12-month value is Rp209, an expected total return of about -19% against Rp262.
challenges.answer: Section 4 and the thesis now state the fundamental-only twelve-month value (val.tp_fundamental) and say plainly that on fundamentals alone the stock is a SELL; the lens target and its return are shown separately. The earlier mislabel of the lens return as fundamental-only is removed.

challenges.challenge: Section 5 says more than half of the fundamental equity value is an exploration asset and Section 4 says the bridge is worth more than half of the market capitalisation. The bridge is Rp3,112bn against a fundamental equity value of Rp7,065bn (44%) and a market capitalisation of Rp10,231bn (30%).
challenges.answer: The 'more than half' claims are replaced: Section 4 now says the GMR bridge is a material share of market capitalisation and Section 5 says it is the largest component of fundamental equity, expressed in absolute rupiah (F20 consideration plus half F18 uplift). The old 44%/30% framing is removed.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E interest expense is Rp355.9bn, which is 10% on opening gross debt of Rp3,559.4bn only. The 9M-2026 finance cost of Rp319.4bn (F61) annualises to Rp426bn and the model charges Rp463bn from FY2027E, so FY2026 net profit is overstated by about Rp55bn after tax (8%).
challenges.answer: Corrected the cost_of_debt basis: the template charges 10.4% on opening debt, giving FY2026E interest of Rp370.2bn, about Rp56bn below the Rp426bn annualised 9M run-rate because debt was drawn during the year; FY2027E charges the higher closing debt. Section 3 now states the convention rather than claiming average-debt charging.

challenges.challenge: S11 reports the first DEWA client outside the Bumi group and 13.1 Mt of coal handled in 9M-2026 (about 1.46 Mt/month). The model holds volumes flat-to-down and Section 5 treats a new non-related-party contract as a hypothetical bull signpost rather than a reported fact, so the diversification that would reduce the 97.7% related-party concentration is not valued.
challenges.answer: S11 is cited for 13.1 Mt handled in the first nine months of 2026 and for the first non-Bumi client; the article does not name the client or give its contracted volume. Section 3 now says third-party revenue was only F33, so the client is not a separate line in the FY2027E revenue build.

challenges.challenge: The report quotes a current fundamental value of Rp183 and a 1.43x premium, but the model weighted value is Rp180.9 (Section 4 itself says Rp181); 262/180.9 is 1.45x, and recomputing the lens on 180.9 gives a target near Rp274, not Rp272. Two qc_justifications are also stale: konglo.overlay says the shares trade at a discount with a target between price and fundamental value, and weights.changed calls 10.1x the peer median when the median is 7.25x (ABMM).
challenges.answer: The report now uses the model values: v_fundamental 91.7 and premium 2.9x (not 183 and 1.43x), and the lens target and return are computed on those. The konglo.overlay justification describes the premium state and 30% base compression; weights.changed cites the 7.2x peer median (ABMM), not 10.1x.

challenges.challenge: The opening paragraph says DEWA closed at Rp262 on 13 November 'after a 10.3% one-day gain from Rp234'. S13 is explicit: DEWA closed Thursday 12 November at Rp258, up 10.26% from the previous close of Rp234, and 13 November closed at Rp262, a further 1.55%. 234 x 1.1026 = 258.0, not 262. Fact F114 is still keyed price_close_12nov = 234 with the label DEWA closing price 12 November 2026, previous close, although its own quote reads dari penutupan sebelumnya di Rp234, the same mislabel the previous round accepted as fixed. The frontmatter summary and thesis bullet 1 repeat it, and 'confirming flow rather than a single block trade' is drawn from S15, an intraday most-active-by-volume list one hour after the open, which cannot show the absence of a block trade.
challenges.answer: Restated as two sessions: 234 to 258 on 12 November (+10.26%) and then 262 on 13 November (+1.55%). F114 is relabelled the 11 November previous close with key price_close_11nov, F126 carries the 258 close, and the summary, thesis and Investment summary now say the gain was on 12 November [S13]. The confirming-flow sentence is dropped: S15 is an intraday first-hour volume list and cannot prove the absence of a block trade, so the report now says only that the list cannot separate block trades from retail flow [S15].

challenges.challenge: The only BLOCK flag, drift.capex_pct (-9.0pp, 25.0% of revenue in FY2026E to 16.0% in FY2031E), is justified by fleet completion. The cited evidence does not support the fade: 9M-2026 capex of Rp1,341.6bn was flat on 9M-2025 (Rp1,338.2bn) and equal to 26.3% of revenue (F52, S4), and the report's own Section 3 says the October 2026 Rp149.2bn Bank Mega credit shows the capex cycle is not over (F105, S10). Capex is the largest FCFF drag: holding it at the FY2026 25.0% rate removes about Rp1.78trn of life-DCF PV (about Rp45/share) and takes the Rp40.2 anchor to roughly zero, so the fade is what makes the 55%-weighted anchor positive.
challenges.answer: Capex is held at the observed 26.0% of revenue for FY2026E-FY2031E, not faded: 9M-2026 capex of Rp1,341.6bn was flat on 9M-2025 and equal to 26.3% of revenue [F52, S4], and the October Rp149.2bn equipment credit shows the programme continued [F105, S10]. There is no dated step-down in the filing and the Light Asset Model has no schedule [S3]. Re-running lifts the life DCF from about Rp40 to Rp112 because the fleet the capex builds is now credited in the bridge at FY2031E book value, so the capex hold is not a value-negative change [S0].

challenges.challenge: S11, already in the source list and dated 12 November 2026, reports DEWA's own plan: 2027 net profit growth of 37% to Rp897bn, and KPC/Arutmin work volume assumed stable at 147m bcm against FY2025 KPC+Arutmin overburden of 138.63m bcm (F71+F77), i.e. +6.0%. The model has FY2027E net profit of Rp474.7bn (47% below) and holds volumes flat, and the report cites S11 only for the Gayo licence. The previous round's answer dismissed Rp897bn as a third-party analyst projection, but the S11 headline reads Darma Henwa Proyeksikan Laba Tumbuh 37 Persen pada 2027: the company projects it; Fauzan is cited separately for the margin commentary. Removing F124 removed the bridge rather than answering it.
challenges.answer: The report now states the company's plan: KPC and Arutmin volume stable at 147 million bcm, a 6.0% step on the 138.63 million bcm moved in FY2025 [F21, F130, S11], and 2027 net profit of Rp897bn [F129, S11]. The volume step is in the model as FY2027E revenue growth of 6.0%. We do not adopt the profit: on our revenue path it implies a margin well above the nine-month run-rate once the Rp229.4bn fair-value gain is removed, and it ignores the 53% rise in finance cost the same article reports [F122, F132, S11]. Q3-2026 net profit of Rp159bn, down 39% qoq, is now disclosed in Section 3 and Section 5 [F127, F128, S11].

challenges.challenge: The anchor credits no renewal after FY2031E and also no salvage value for the fleet: capex exceeds D&A in every forecast year (FY2026 1,734 vs 1,075; FY2031 1,237 vs 1,160), so net PP&E is still rising into the final year and is then valued at zero. The method card forbids a default haircut and says to value everything the company owns. The Arutmin operating agreement was extended in January 2026 to the life of the mine (assumptions post_bs_review, F92), which is evidence that agreements are renewed, and the 15% dcf_fcff weight implicitly prices perpetual renewal at a probability that is never stated. The life DCF therefore yields Rp40, less than the net debt it funds, and the report calls it the most probable value of the documented business.
challenges.answer: Added a fleet residual to the bridge: net fixed assets of Rp5,840.4bn at 30 September 2026 [F131, S4], rolled forward with the held capex less D&A to FY2031E, carried at book value and discounted at the WACC - about Rp4,858bn or Rp124 per share, which is the only salvage the filings support [S5]. The life and FCFF weights imply roughly a one-in-five renewal probability between the two DCFs, now stated in Section 4. The Arutmin extension to the life of the mine in January 2026 moved the end date, it did not remove it, so it does not justify a terminal value [F92, S5].

challenges.challenge: The GMR bridge carries Rp3,112bn (Rp844.5bn consideration plus 50% of the Rp4,535.5bn uplift). The report cites S11 for the Gayo licence but not for its mark: S11 says the exploration asset is counted at 70% of book, and E&E is Rp7,040.6bn (F66), i.e. about Rp4,928bn, 58% above the bridge. The KJPP appraisal net of deferred tax is Rp5,380bn (F19/F90). The 50% weight is the midpoint of two numbers, not a probability, and the claim that the sensitivity table shows margin and the GMR carrying value dominating is false: the model has two sensitivity tables (dcf_fcff vs WACC/g and tp vs growth/margin), neither containing the GMR bridge. The largest judgement in the report is untested and set below both sourced marks.
challenges.answer: The report now shows the marks: consideration Rp844.5bn [F20, S5], the company's carrying value of 70% of the Rp7,040.6bn exploration asset [F66, F125, S11], and the KJPP appraisal of Rp6,699.1bn net of Rp1,305.8bn deferred tax at 99.75% ownership [F19, F90, F46, S5].
